source.description:
PROBLEM: The PR #190 security audit found a separate CI trust-boundary defect: pull_request-controlled repository code runs on persistent self-hosted runners, and the OSV PR job also carries pull-request comment write authority. A malicious or compromised PR can execute on a trusted host and potentially abuse writable credentials. This concern is real but intentionally out of scope for PR #190 and must ship independently.

SUCCESS: Open one separate focused security PR, based on current master after PR #190 lands, that prevents untrusted pull_request code from executing on self-hosted runners and removes writable-token exposure from untrusted execution. Preserve trusted push/schedule hard gates and useful PR scan feedback. Enumerate equivalent pull_request jobs first so the fix closes the root trust-boundary class rather than only one YAML line; keep the resulting diff minimal and explicitly justify any job left unchanged.

SCRUTINY: critical

SCOPE: .github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml and any other .github/workflows/*.yml jobs proven to execute pull_request-controlled code on self-hosted runners; least-privilege GitHub permissions/comment handoff; bounded workflow contract tests or static assertions. Begin with an evidence-only workflow inventory before implementation.

NON_GOALS: No changes to PR #190's OSV 0/1 allowlist, classifier semantics, forensic launch_mode fix, application runtime, specialist prompts/assets, npm publication, deployment, or unrelated CI modernization.

CONSTRAINTS: Separate branch/PR only; fork from master after #190 merge. Untrusted PR execution must use ephemeral GitHub-hosted isolation. Privileged comment/update logic must not execute PR-controlled scripts or workflow definitions with write credentials; use a trusted base-code handoff or remove nonessential commenting if that is the smallest safe solution. Pin actions, preserve protected-branch scanning, no force-push/rebase/history rewrite. GitNexus may not index workflows; document that and use exact workflow/test evidence. Independent seconder, test, security, obligations, pr-reviewer, CI, and deploy-monitor gates before closure.

VALIDATION: Static/adversarial tests prove pull_request jobs cannot select self-hosted labels, writable token is absent from untrusted steps, trusted push/schedule behavior remains, and sanitized outputs cannot inject privileged actions. Run workflow syntax/lint, targeted tests, full relevant CI, security audit, reviewer, and post-merge deploy/artifact verification.

OUTPUT: Workflow inventory, chosen minimal trust split, PR URL/head, tests/security/reviewer/CI evidence, residual risks, and post-merge deploy-monitor verdict. Parent orchestrator alone merges and closes.
source.notes:
DESIGN GATE: exact current-master workflow inventory found 5 vulnerable workflow files (gitleaks, osv-scanner, package-payload, semgrep, telemetry-contract) and one already-safe runner workflow (pi-compat). Minimal separate PR: conditional ubuntu for PR paths, protected push/schedule keep CI_RUNNER; remove OSV comment + PR write token and unused gitleaks write permission; persist-credentials:false on all PR checkouts; explicit contents:read; static policy test enumerating all PR workflows. Generic design hazards and residual risks recorded in child .3.
Operator explicitly accepted PR193 residual PR-controlled workflow risk and directed merge now with immutable runner enforcement deferred to unitAI-tmeqw.12. Revised merge gate assesses delta: PR193 must materially reduce current exposure, introduce no new HIGH/CRITICAL risk, retain green CI/tests, and receive security PASS_WITH_NOTES + pr-reviewer approval; residual remains open.

source.description:
PROBLEM: Final security audit d6aea2 found CRITICAL PR193-SEC-01 (90% confidence): PR #193 changes current workflow definitions and adds a mutable in-PR test, but a malicious PR can change its own workflow `runs-on` to the online repository-level `specialists-runner`; GitHub assigns the runner before the PR-controlled policy test runs. Current external state: repo runner id 1155 `specialists-runner` is online with labels self-hosted/Linux/X64/mercury-lite/specialists; it is repository-level (org Default group has zero runners and unrestricted workflows); fork approval policy is first_time_contributors.

SUCCESS: Immutable external enforcement prevents any pull_request ref/workflow from assigning the specialists self-hosted runner before PR code executes. Then an adversarial PR/workflow scheduling test proves blocked, trusted main/schedule behavior is verified per chosen design, security re-audit passes zero HIGH/CRITICAL, and PR #193 may proceed.

SCRUTINY: critical

SCOPE: Choose one explicitly authorized production remediation: (A) retire/unregister the repo-level specialists runner and route trusted push/schedule jobs to ubuntu-latest; or (B) migrate it to an org runner group restricted to exact specialists workflow files at refs/heads/master. Update managed infra/service config and workflow code/tests as required, with rollback evidence.

NON_GOALS: Do not merge PR #193, weaken/waive the finding, rely on mutable in-PR tests as enforcement, change unrelated runners/repos, publish npm, or alter production runner state without explicit operator authorization.

CONSTRAINTS: Production-impacting and CRITICAL: warn operator, obtain explicit authorization for A or B, use isolated tests, preserve backups/rollback, adversarial security test, independent security re-audit. Parent orchestrator alone merges/closes anchor.

VALIDATION: GitHub API runner/group state before/after; service/registration state; fork/PR attempt selecting self-hosted must remain unassigned/rejected; trusted main/schedule expected job passes; security auditor exact recheck.

OUTPUT: Chosen design/authorization, config/code PRs, before/after policy evidence, rollback, adversarial test, re-audit verdict.
